profile.style: Emotional breakup and glow-up posts using sad audio, short captions, and self-improvement hashtags, with the app sitting behind a confidence/attractiveness angle.
works: Breakup + self-love framing: 307,800 views and 148,400 views were both tagged around breakup/selflove
Emotional Tom Odell sound: their two strongest videos used “Another Love” and got 3.9× and 1.9× their usual views
Glow-up / discipline angle: the best video used #discipline and #selflove and got 20,000 likes, 858 shares, and 2,283 saves
Simple emotional captions beat app-forward posting: the best posts feel like a breakup story, not a product pitch
doesnt: Direct question caption did not land: “Should he get her back?” got 583 views, under 0.1× usual
Generic healing caption was weaker: “choosing yourself” got 8,506 views, 0.1× usual
Moving away from the proven breakup/glow-up setup seems to drop views

ideas.so: Your best post was the breakup + self-love + discipline setup at 307,800 views, 3.9× your usual. The weaker 583-view post asked a direct question, so make this one feel like a story instead of a poll.
why: It builds from your 307,800-view breakup/self-love/discipline post instead of moving into a totally new lane.
It avoids the direct question format that got 583 views by making the question live in the caption, not the whole idea.
It keeps the app useful but not too salesy, matching the posts where simple emotional captions did better.
ideas.hook: "She left, so he rebuilt his voice."
ideas.sound: Another Love (slowed down original sound) · Tom Odell
ideas.format: Emotional breakup glow-up caption video with the app behind the confidence story

script.say: He didn’t beg. He got quiet.
script.shot: A simple emotional text screen over a moody clip or still.
script.point: Start with the breakup pain, not the app.

script.say: First thing he fixed was how he sounded when he spoke.
script.shot: Phone screen with a voice-confidence check or practice view, kept subtle.
script.point: Connect the glow-up to confidence and voice.

script.say: Ten minutes a day. Slower words. Better posture. Less panic.
script.shot: Quick cuts of a short routine: notes, mirror, walking, app in the background.
script.point: Make it feel like discipline, not revenge.

script.say: Not to win her back. To stop sounding like he lost himself.
script.shot: Clean final text over a calm, confident shot.

ideas.caption: Would you start with your voice or your body first? Comment one.
ideas.post_time: Tuesday 8:00 PM, when your audience is free and likely scrolling breakup/self-improvement content
ideas.make_it_yours: Change one thing from the old winner: make the glow-up specifically about voice confidence, so it feels like a new chapter, not a repost.

ideas.so: The bigger breakup creator’s reassurance video got 5.1M views and 74,704 saves with a calm “you’re going to be okay” voiceover. That format fits your audience because they already respond to breakup emotion, but you can make it yours by tying the calm-down moment to voice control and confidence.
why: The borrowed format is proven in the niche: a direct comfort talk got 5.1M views and very high saves.
It serves followers better than a one-off meme because people may follow for repeated calm-down/confidence help.
It adapts the idea to your app’s lane by making voice control part of the healing moment.
ideas.hook: "If you want to text them tonight, pause."
ideas.sound: your voiceover over a soft sad instrumental
ideas.format: Calm breakup reassurance voiceover with a subtle voice-confidence exercise

script.say: If your thumb is on their name right now, wait.
script.shot: Text on screen with a phone nearby, no need to show messages.
script.point: Name the exact moment your viewer is in.

script.say: You’re not weak. Your body just wants the pain to stop fast.
script.shot: Simple slow-moving background or dark selfie-style setup.

script.say: Put the phone down. Take one breath. Say one sentence out loud slowly.
script.shot: A short voice practice screen, note, or timer.
script.point: Give them a tiny action that fits your niche.

script.say: If you can control your voice in this moment, you can control the next choice too.
script.shot: Final text with a calm confidence line.
script.point: Turn the action into a confidence win.

script.say: Comment the word you need to hear tonight.
script.shot: Plain end card with the comment prompt.

ideas.caption: Comment the word you need to hear tonight.
ideas.post_time: Thursday 9:00 PM, when people are winding down and breakup thoughts hit harder
ideas.make_it_yours: Keep the feeling of comfort, but use your own short voice exercise so it does not become a copy of the original reassurance video.

ideas.so: #sad is early in your niche data, with 3 videos this week and 0 last week. Your strongest posts already use sad emotional audio and breakup framing, so this is the cleanest trend to ride without leaving your lane.
why: #sad is early this week, so it matches the current niche movement without forcing a new topic.
Your two best posts were emotional breakup/glow-up posts, so this trend fits what already worked for you.
The caption asks for personal comments, while the video itself stays story-led instead of repeating the 583-view direct-question approach.
ideas.hook: "The sad part is, the glow-up starts after."
ideas.sound: soft sad audio or Another Love if it still fits the edit
ideas.format: Short sad-to-discipline glow-up post built for #sad and #breakup

script.say: The sad part is, you don’t change while they’re watching.
script.shot: Minimal text over a quiet, emotional visual.
script.point: Make the first line hurt a little.

script.say: You change after the call ends. After the crying. After nobody checks on you.
script.shot: Small routine moments: water, notes, walk, voice practice.
script.point: Flip sadness into a private routine.

script.say: Then one day your face looks calmer, and your voice sounds steadier.
script.shot: App or voice practice screen shown briefly, not as the main sales point.
script.point: Bring in the voice/attractiveness angle softly.

script.say: That’s the glow-up nobody sees coming.
script.point: End with a commentable identity line.

ideas.caption: What part of your glow-up are you keeping private? Comment it.
ideas.post_time: Saturday 11:00 AM, when your audience has time to save/share self-improvement posts
ideas.make_it_yours: Use your real product angle only as the quiet confidence tool in the middle, not as the headline.

plan.summary: Post one direct sequel to the breakup/self-love format that already worked, one calming breakup voiceover borrowed from a bigger healing creator, and one early #sad post that fits your emotional style. All three keep the app behind the confidence angle instead of making the app the main character.
plan.headline: Your own numbers say people come for *breakup glow-up*, not app-first questions: the two strongest posts hit 307,800 and 148,400 views. This week, make a 3-post mini-series around *the voice/confidence glow-up after they leave*.

patterns.title: Breakup plus self-love is your clearest winner.
patterns.detail: The two posts tagged around breakup, glow-up, motivation and self-love reached 307,800 and 148,400 views, both above your usual 78,453.

patterns.title: Questions are weaker when they become the whole post.
patterns.detail: “Should he get her back?” reached 583 views, while the stronger posts used simple emotional framing instead of asking the viewer to decide the story.

patterns.title: Sad audio helps most when the topic is still breakup glow-up.
patterns.detail: Another Love was on both a 307,800-view post and the 583-view post, so the sound alone is not enough. The topic and framing did the heavier lifting.
